leaves.t: YouTube is the main screen for kids in the family living room; kids under 12 watch mostly there.
Kids Shorts are huge: 8 of the 10 most-viewed videos on all platforms in 2025 were kids YouTube Shorts.
Indian family/kids channels dominate YouTube Shorts; often 19-27 of the weekly global top 50 channels are Indian.
Kids/baby content gets about 71K views per Instagram post, similar to TikTok and far above typical brand YouTube posts.
Instagram's 2026 algorithm favours original Reels; a Reel detected as reposted from TikTok can be pushed down.
Vertical 9:16 beats square by 2-3x on short-form platforms.
On Netflix, CoComelon has dropped out of the kids top 10 in 2026 and its spin offs did not reverse the slide; analysts call it nursery rhyme fatigue.
YouTube born kids creators are now Netflix hits: Ms. Rachel 208M hours in H1 2026, Sheriff Labrador 111M, Danny Go! 54M from one short season.
Danny Go!, a high energy movement and dance along show from YouTube, stayed in Netflix's global top 10 for three months after its April 2026 launch.
Sheriff Labrador (BabyBus, China) grew 784% on Netflix after expanding from Latin America worldwide, proof that a Chinese 3D animal kids brand travels globally.
Bluey was the most streamed title in the US for the second year in 2025 (about 45 billion minutes); calm, funny family play beats frantic content on the living room TV.
Spotify added a global setting (Sep 2026) so parents can keep kids and family music out of their own recommendations and Wrapped; kids songs are clearly a big share of family streaming.
Nonsense chant songs spread among Gen Alpha on TikTok and Reels: 'Chicken Banana', a techno track by a Swedish channel, became a dance trend and then a playground catchphrase.
KPop Demon Hunters showed a kids music franchise can keep growing long after launch; K pop style songs and dance are a strong worldwide kid taste in 2025 and 2026.

YouTube added Shorts series with seasons and episodes (23 Sep 2026) and custom Shorts thumbnails (Jul 2026); the dislike button left Shorts in Jun 2026, replaced by 'Not interested' and 'Don't recommend this channel'.

About 55% of Reel views come from non followers, and DM sends are weighted roughly 3 to 5 times more than likes for reaching non followers; 3 to 4 strong Reels a week in one consistent niche is the suggested cadence.
Instagram flags accounts as 'aggregators' with reduced non follower reach when most posts in 30 days reuse 70% or more of another creator's visuals or audio; our own original songs keep us safe.
Instagram Trial Reels (accounts with 1,000+ followers) show a Reel to non followers first, a free way to test two hooks for the same song before sharing to followers.
Reels can be up to 20 minutes for eligible accounts, but only Reels up to 3 minutes are recommended to non followers.
YouTube reaches 67% of US kids aged 2 to 5, 78% of 6 to 9 and 80% of 10 to 12, far ahead of tablet games, streaming services and other social video apps.

Kids streaming trends for 2026: learning wrapped in stories (science, nature, feelings), interactive quizzes and choices, shorter flexible episodes, characters from many cultures and family types, and nature and recycling themes.
On Netflix, PAW Patrol led kids hours in H2 2025 and Gabby's Dollhouse led 2025 overall; preschool is now so crowded that new IP needs strong marketing as well as strong content to break in.
UK 8 to 14 year olds spend about 3 hours a day online; YouTube reaches almost all of them in a month and Roblox is the top games app at 61% reach.

In Tubefilter's most subscribed chart for the week of 8 Nov 2026, 37 of the top 50 channels are mainly Shorts channels and India has 14 of them, so Shorts remain the fastest subscriber engine worldwide.

After YouTube Kids entry, PlayToys and Play Dolls launched Shorts for the first time and reached about 1.18M views with 27 to 30 second average watch, so Kids app access and Shorts work best together.

Instagram's Your Algorithm lets viewers add or remove topics they want; it started on Reels (Dec 2025), reached all English speakers (Jan 2026), Explore (15 Apr 2026) and the main Feed (Jun 2026), so each Reel should signal one clear topic like kids songs or kids dance.

Reels guidance for 2026: show motion or on screen text within about half a second, use keyword rich captions rather than piles of hashtags, and add short on screen text so Instagram's AI can read the topic.
Instagram near duplicate penalties (70% or more shared visuals or audio) last from 24 hours to 30 days and cut only non follower reach; since Apr 2026 they also apply to photos and carousels.

Reels advice is about 90% niche consistency; mixing Hindi Didi story Reels with English dance songs on one account may blur our topic signal, so a separate story account or a steady weekly slot is worth testing.
leaves.src: SocialPilot Sep 2026 with our posting mix

leaves.t: Baby Shark joined Spotify's Billions Club in May 2026 with about 137M streams in a year and about 400K a day from 23M listeners, led by the US, UK, Australia and Canada, so audio streaming of kids songs is strongest in high paying English markets.

Netflix's global top 10 for 14 to 20 Sep 2026 held Gabby's Dollhouse S14 (best debut since S8), YouTube creator Mark Rober's CrunchLabs, A Minecraft Movie and KPop Demon Hunters still charting in week 65.

KIDZ BOP (11B+ streams) reaches Gen Alpha on Roblox by placing its album inside a popular obstacle course game (Really Easy Obby, about 580K daily visits) where kids collect music notes while songs play.
YouTube's recommender has two goals: help each viewer find what they want and maximise long-term satisfaction; in 2026 satisfaction (surveys, rewatches, 'not interested') outweighs raw watch time.
Recommendations are not one system: Home, Suggested, Search, Shorts feed and Subscriptions each rank with different signals; Suggested looks mainly at the video being watched now.
Long-form: click-through rate on thumbnail+title and average view duration work as a pair; the thumbnail must deliver what it promises or satisfaction drops.
Shorts run on a separate engine: each Short goes to a seed audience (a few hundred viewers); if they watch instead of swiping away, reach widens in waves.
Shorts key signals: viewed vs swiped away, watch-through %, loops/replays and shares; benchmark about 65% average view duration for Shorts under 30 s, about 50% for 30-60 s.
The first 1.5 to 3 seconds of a Short decide most swipe-aways, so the opening frame must already be the hook.
Since 1 Oct 2026 YouTube's recommender gives more reach to original Shorts; reused or inauthentic content is reviewed at channel level.
Views now count from the first frame (Shorts since Mar 2025, all formats since Aug 2026), so raw views look bigger; engaged views and retention are the real health metrics.
Made-for-kids videos lose comments, notification bell, cards/end screens and personalised ads, so discovery relies even more on watch behaviour, Search and Suggested.
YouTube Kids app recommendations come from what each child profile watched and searched; homepage shelves are series, music, learning, discovery and games.
New channels typically get cautious distribution for the first few months until the system has performance history; consistency builds that trust.
Instagram Reels rank on watch time first, then sends (DM shares) per reach, then likes per reach; sends matter most for reaching non-followers; reposts and watermarks are demoted.
For kids songs, compilations and 'Up Next' sessions matter: if the next suggested video is yours, you keep the session; stitch 5-6 songs into mega mixes led by the best performer.

Because made for kids videos lose end screens, cards and the bell, keyword named playlists are the main discovery tool; descriptions should link to the first video of a related playlist so autoplay continues in order.

For kids and teens long form, Friday is the best upload day and Wednesday the weakest, a +379% gap (the biggest of any niche); peak slots are 16:00 UTC and 23:00 UTC, and 10 to 20 minute videos fit best.

24/7 live streams of the back catalogue gave a kids channel 41.9% of its watch time from under a fifth of its views, at 66% higher RPM; big kids channels run 4 to 5 streams at once like mini TV stations.
A kids stream view earned about 1.45 USD per 1,000 versus 0.43 for a normal video view; on one 8M channel streams were only 4% of views while total channel views grew 53%.
In a 282 channel study, large kids channels earned the most total revenue at 16 or more videos a month, so our 14 a week cadence is in the winning range.
Once a channel is in the YouTube Kids app it can become the main source: YouTube Kids brought 67% of traffic for Baby Ben en Espanol and 68 to 78% for the BIBO toy channels.
Since Jan 2026 parents can cap the Shorts feed for kids and teens, even to zero, so Shorts cannot be the only growth engine; long form and playlists must carry the channel.

YouTube keeps autoplay off by default and Take a Break and Bedtime reminders on for signed in under 18s, so continuation to our next video cannot be assumed; long compilations and playlists inside one session matter more.

YouTube's Todd Beaupre (Sep 2026): a new upload's first hour is not a subscriber test; it is shown to mixed audiences including people who never watched the channel, and each audience is judged separately.
leaves.src: Creator Insider via PPC Land, Sep 2026

leaves.t: Even a channel's best videos are usually picked by only about 10% or fewer of subscribers who see them in the feed, so low subscriber click rate is normal and not a penalty.
leaves.src: Creator Insider via PPC Land, Sep 2026

leaves.t: Recommendations are built fresh per viewer at the start of each session; no single metric decides, and the weight of clicks, watch time, surveys and likes changes by person, device and moment.
leaves.src: Creator Insider via PPC Land, Sep 2026

leaves.t: In the YouTube Kids app, new child profiles get no personal recommendations until they build history, so they browse curated shelves (series, music, learning, discovery, games); being in the music and learning shelves is key for a new song channel.
leaves.src: Team YouTube FAQ via PPC Land, Apr 2026

leaves.t: YouTube's Shorts lead says there is no ideal Short length, posting time or daily quota and hashtags are optional; a Short that stalls needs a fresh new Short, because deleting and reposting can be read as spam.

WOA Song Spanish (kids songs) deleted long videos that skirted kids policies and posted 31 quality checked Shorts in Q4 2025 (up from 8); views jumped from 27M to 1.46B in one quarter, with Shorts giving over 98% of views.

Weak or policy risky old videos can hold a kids channel back; cleaning the library and applying kids quality rules (educational value, positive role models, clear visuals, correct metadata) preceded the breakout.

A kids channel that cut long uploads from 21 to 11 a quarter, doubled Shorts cut from its funniest long form moments and moved to 4K TV friendly picture and sound grew revenue 34% while views grew only 5%.
Kids channels see a holiday view spike in late November and early December, so the next three weeks are the time to post more Shorts.

In Sept 2026 YouTube's inauthentic content enforcement suspended channels of long sleep music and prayer compilations built on one template; our lullaby and mega mix compilations must vary songs, visuals and order, not repeat one template.

Since 22 Oct 2026 US viewers can save up to 3 custom Home feeds and the mobile Home top bar has separate Live, Music and Movies and TV feeds, with Subscriptions moved there; clear music metadata helps songs land in the Music feed.

Ask YouTube (conversational answers on web, mobile and TV in the US since 12 Oct 2026) can answer a query without a click, so titles and descriptions should match the exact questions parents ask (for example a song to help a toddler brush teeth).

Creator analysis since late 2025 says the recommender ranks by expected satisfied watch time per click rather than watch time per impression, and older Shorts that ran for years lost distribution, so a steady flow of fresh Shorts beats relying on the back catalogue.

Creator data from over 1,000 channels suggests Home now shows as few as 2 long form videos per row with reserved Shorts slots (down from about 6), so long form songs depend more on Suggested, Search and playlists than on Home.
At Made on YouTube (23 Sep 2026) YouTube announced video A/B testing, AI feedback on drafts in Ask Studio, Shorts series and a live auto dubbing pilot for early 2027.

The Melobies, an energetic nursery rhyme channel, grew subscribers about 9 times (917%) after a package of fixes: listing in YouTube Kids, more expressive characters with high contrast simple mobile thumbnails, keyword matched titles, playlists grouped by theme and 24/7 best of streams; its top video then hit 3.5M views, triple its norm.
An audit of The Melobies flagged poorly organised compilations as a watch time leak; compilations should open with the strongest song and keep one theme so viewers stay through.

Sandy the Sticker (near 1M subs) went from 1 manual to 16 automated 24/7 streams, added Shorts cut from high energy long form moments and raised long uploads 44% in a quarter: watch time rose 31%, average view duration 1:36 to 2:06, revenue 63%.

Across these kids cases, 24/7 live streams of the back catalogue are repeatedly named the main growth driver once a channel has a few dozen strong songs, so a looping stream is worth starting after we pass about 50 songs.
Cocomelon is still the biggest kids channel (about 200M subs, about 229B views); its top video is Wheels on the Bus (8.4B).
Baby Shark Dance (Pinkfong) is the most-viewed YouTube video ever, about 17.5B views (Nov 2026).
Next tier: ChuChu TV (about 98M), Super Simple Songs, Infobells Hindi (about 73M), Vlad and Niki, Kids Diana Show, Like Nastya.
Ms. Rachel (live, slow, speech-focused) became a top-4 Netflix kids show in her first year; creator-led preschool content is rising.
Multi-language dubbing is a key growth lever for the biggest kids channels (Diana, Nastya, ChuChu's 12 language channels).
Long compilations and 24/7 live streams of the back catalogue keep old songs earning views.
Cocomelon's biggest buckets are fresh spins on classic rhymes and originals that blend a classic with a modern hook; its average video length grew to about 20 minutes (compilations).
Seven of the 10 most-watched YouTube Kids videos of 2019 were songs/nursery rhymes, and the top one was a 36-minute song compilation.
A proven repeatable formula: a familiar song or character placed in a new world or holiday ('X visits the Magic Forest / Christmas'), packaged as sing-along.
Bebefinn (Pinkfong) is about 84M subscribers and 65 billion views brand wide; its Netflix series hit No. 1 kids title in 12 countries and an Amazon Kids+ series is coming.

Bebefinn's main English channel (37M subs) gets about 370M views a month; its top videos are a wake up morning routine (775M), a Baby Shark crossover, a mix compilation and a 'Run Away Baby Car' chase.
Bebefinn's newest uploads are pretend play job stories (car mechanics fixing a car) with emoji led titles and a brand hashtag, posted about 4 to 5 times a week.

Lalafun, a 3D nursery rhyme channel started in Oct 2022, reached 15M subscribers and 11.6 billion views in about 4 years at 3 to 4 uploads a week, now 600 to 700M views a month: a new 3D channel can break through fast.

Lalafun's biggest hits are animal twists on public domain rhymes with a learning tag: Wheels on the Bus Animal Version (955M), 5 Little Ducks Learn Colors (726M), Old MacDonald with Safari Animals, Counting 10 Little Pandas.
Lalafun's latest titles frame a small mystery the song solves ('Where did the animals' colours go?'), turning a colours song into a rescue story.

Bebefinn launched with a crossover starring the company's existing mega hit character, and that episode is still its second most viewed; reusing our own recurring friends across songs builds the same pull.

VocaVoca (US, kids songs, mostly Shorts) hit #23 in Tubefilter's worldwide top 50 with about 527M weekly views; its monthly views rose from about 0.5B in May to 2.9B in Oct 2026 with 1.56M new subscribers that month.

VocaVoca's biggest songs teach healthy habits and safety: going to the dentist (164M), caring for a baby, police officer job song, stranger safety, and a buckle up song in the 'no no, I don't want to' refusal format, plus new good manners cartoons.

In the 8 Nov 2026 Tubefilter top 50, Indian family channels rode Diwali: Baccha Mat Bolna (#28, 415M weekly views) mixes festival vlogs with childhood games like 'the floor is lava', and Paintellectual PriyA (#40) teaches young viewers to draw festive lamps.

ChuChu TV (Chennai, founded 2013) reports 180M+ digital subscribers and 110 billion views and signed a worldwide Netflix deal in Sep 2026 for Surprise Eggs, Drawing with ChuChu, Colors in FunZone and Nursery Rhymes in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.

ChuChu TV is turning a YouTube song channel into a global preschool franchise (licensing, toys, publishing, live shows) through a North American partner, showing an Indian 3D song brand can scale worldwide.
ChuChu TV's Netflix collections are learning formats (colours, drawing, surprise reveals, rhymes), confirming that colour and draw along songs travel across languages.
Cocomelon's main channel is at about 203M subscribers in Nov 2026, still the largest kids channel.

Kids channels in that week's top 50 subscriber gainers: Pokemon Kids TV (#23, about 400K a week), Cadel and Mia (#37, Australian family) and VocaVoca kids songs (#45, about 300K a week, steady for weeks).

Pokemon Kids TV (44.8M subs, about 71M views in 28 days) gets its biggest song hits from short dance songs built around one named character (One Pikachu dance song, 226M; Scorbunny Dancing, 94M), proving a signature character dance is evergreen.

Sasha Show (Russian language) jumped 9.5M subscribers in Oct 2026 with sensational Shorts using famous borrowed characters (Sonic, PAW Patrol, Ladybug) and scary or naughty titles; this is the low quality pattern YouTube's kids principles penalise, so it is not a model for us.

Animaj (owner of Pocoyo) launched Ozzy Fox in Jul 2026 on YouTube and YouTube Kids: each episode centres on one original song that turns an everyday routine into a mission; the first two episodes passed 1.5M views in under five days.

Super Simple Songs (47.3M subs) rose from about 490M monthly views in Jan 2026 to about 590M in Oct 2026 while gaining only 100 to 200K subscribers a month: a deep song library keeps compounding views long after upload.

Super Simple Songs' all time leaders are puppet led action and counting songs (500 Ducks, 214M; If You're Happy and You Know It Spin Around, 176M; Five Little Speckled Frogs, 164M), and its newest release (5 Nov 2026) is a wash your hands and face routine song with about 900K views in 9 days.

A Little Angel channel (about 7.3M subs) posting daily in Oct 2026 got only 7K to 30K views on most play and adventure episodes, while its Brush Your Teeth healthy habit song got 96K, so routine songs beat generic play stories even for a big brand.

On that Little Angel channel the dance Short (Do the Daddy and Jill Dance) drew the most likes of the recent uploads (344 versus under 100 for most long videos), backing family dance moments as Short material.
Upbeat tempo drives movement; Baby Shark sits at about 117 BPM. Aim for 110-125 BPM for dance songs.
Heavy repetition of a 1-2 bar melodic hook and of whole sections is the common thread of mega-hits.
Narrow, simple melody (about 5 notes) lets small kids sing along, which rewards them and drives replays.
Family words (baby, mommy, daddy, grandma) create an emotional bond with the song.
Story moments with tempo change (speed up for 'run away', slow for 'safe at last') let kids act the song out.
A key change up a half-step near the end lifts energy without making it harder to sing.
Cocomelon uses song duos (call and answer parts) and reuses the same melodies with simple lyrics.
Children of all ages in studies prefer major-key songs over minor-key songs, and familiarity with a song strongly raises how much they like it.
leaves.src: Dobrota & Gusic study, J. Elementary Education

leaves.t: Preschoolers (5-6) like many styles but rate a children's song sung by a child highest; a kid lead voice beats an adult voice.
Kids aged 4-6 in the US and Poland prefer songs they already know with a fast tempo and a strong beat; they react by moving and drawing rather than describing.
leaves.src: Vasil & Kondracka-Szala, J. Popular Music Education 2025

leaves.t: Over 80% of popular and kids music is in major keys and 2/4 or 4/4 time; staying there keeps songs instantly singable.
Super Simple Songs builds songs on Total Physical Response: every lyric pairs with an action, tempo slowed so toddlers can act each word, with short pauses for kids to echo.
leaves.src: Super Simple about page / SSS analyses

leaves.t: Call-and-response (riddle style 'I see something...?' or echo lines) gives kids a safe place to join in and a small reward when they answer.
Calm songs for wind-down sit around 60-70 BPM (resting heart rate); keep a bedtime/lullaby lane alongside 110-125 BPM dance songs.
Nonsense syllables like 'doo doo doo' make songs singable for pre-verbal toddlers; Baby Shark's family call-and-response is the model.

Babies recognise music by 3 months, but only by 12 months do they move differently to real songs than to scrambled ones, mostly with the upper body, and none keep the beat; simple bounce and arm moves suit the youngest viewers.
Higher pitched music drew a stronger brain response at 6 months and slightly more movement at every age tested; bright high register sounds (bells, glockenspiel, xylophone, kid voices) grab babies.
Newborns already anticipate a steady beat while melody is learned slowly, so a strong clap or drum pattern is the first hook for the youngest; the melody hook comes second.
A 16 country study of over 2,000 babies found they listen longer to sing song baby talk (slower, melodic, simple words) than to adult speech; spoken lines in songs should use that sing song delivery.
From about 10 months many babies prefer the voices of other young children, which backs a kid lead singer; but preferences vary by culture, so no single voice style is universal.
Pinkfong's Bebefinn runs on near constant looping songs in short segments that parents use as a 'one more song' timer, with a sibling trio and supportive parents.

Veteran kids songwriter Laurie Berkner builds audience participation and movement into the song itself and avoids talking down to kids; songs that let kids move when told to sit still are the ones they love.

An 8 week rhythm and movement program (clapping, tapping sticks, body percussion in time with others) gave 200+ four year olds better social skills and fewer behaviour problems; clap along parts make a song valued by parents and teachers.

Danny Go! builds its catalogue as dance games: freeze dances, fast versus slow animal dances, pretend danger games ('sharks in the water'), 'hyperspeed' remixes and long brain break compilations used in classrooms.
leaves.src: Danny Go! video titles / parent reviews, 2026

leaves.t: Parents say kids love songs about their favourite things (garbage trucks, diggers, bugs, trains) and useful songs like a clean up tune that actually gets them tidying.

CoComelon treats music as the main teaching tool: episodes open with a song and transitions are sung; since 2026 learning experts from UCLA's Center for Scholars and Storytellers shape its season goals and scripts.
Babies who were sung to often by 6 months had larger vocabularies at 14 months, and a 2025 review of six studies found songs help word learning and speech fluency.
leaves.src: J. Child Language / review via The Signal, Apr 2026

leaves.t: Young children's ability to detect rhythm and patterns is linked to grammar and early reading skills, so steady rhymes and predictable line patterns help learning as well as catchiness.

In a 2026 eLife study (79 infants aged 3 to 12 months) no baby moved in time with the beat; their movement followed changes in loudness and intensity, so clear loud then soft, big then small contrasts drive baby movement more than a precise groove.

Babies aged 9 to 12 months listened longer, stayed calmer and danced more to familiar songs, even when sung by a stranger at a different tempo and pitch, so re singing our best melodies in new versions keeps their pull.

Billboard's Kid Albums chart in early November is topped by A Charlie Brown Christmas (gentle jazz piano), followed by movie musicals; CoComelon, Pinkfong and Super Simple Songs are the only YouTube born brands in its top 15, so a soft jazzy holiday sound is a proven family taste.
Baby Shark's lasting success is credited to a simple melody, simple choreography and cross generational appeal; songs parents also enjoy get played on family speakers for years.
Kids like to see other kids dancing on screen; the version of Baby Shark with real kids dancing is the one that went viral.
Big eyes, round geometric shapes and saturated colours attract young viewers.
YouTube-native kids content is about twice as fast and brighter than broadcast kids TV.
Cocomelon cuts every 1-3 s, but experts criticise this as over-stimulating; parents move kids to calmer shows like Bluey.
Pixar-like rounded 3D style is proven with young kids.
Character-led storytelling is beating plain tutorial/fact content in 2026; recurring characters are the long-term asset.
Kids copy what they see: Ms. Rachel's success rests on direct eye contact, big gestures paired with every word, and pauses that invite kids to answer.
Direct address (characters talk to the viewer), call-and-response prompts and on-screen action cues (clap, jump) turn watching into joining in (Blue's Clues, Dora, Wiggles).
Blue's Clues' famous four-beat pause gives kids time to answer; brief silent beats after a question raise participation.
Children respond to big, expressive, non-threatening eyes, in thumbnails as much as in the video.
Kids thumbnails should avoid shocked, crying, scared or panicked faces, scary monsters and danger; YouTube's classifiers read thumbnails and titles before any human does.
leaves.src: AIR Media-Tech kids channel case study, Apr 2026

leaves.t: Keep thumbnail text to three words or fewer, bright high-contrast colours, one clear subject.

YouTube's Test and Compare (up to 3 titles or thumbnails, winner picked by watch time share, not clicks) cannot be used on made for kids videos, so we must test thumbnails by hand, one change at a time.
Kids thumbnail formula: one happy face, one clear action, one recognisable object, plain bright background and very little text; if a thumbnail trips two or more warning signs, redo it.
Kids titles work best as a story moment hook plus one niche keyword, with only one or two capitalised words and one or two emojis; the title should add to the thumbnail, not repeat it.

Parents search by age and moment: YouTube suggested phrases in Oct 2026 include 'nursery rhymes for toddlers', 'learn numbers 1-10' and 'bedtime stories for preschoolers'; put those phrases in titles, descriptions and playlist names.
Short clips of 15 to 30 seconds help discovery only when the character is distinctive enough to make viewers seek more; recurring, recognisable Bro Bros looks are what turn Shorts into subscribers.
A 7M subscriber Arabic kids channel whose recommendations fell 91% recovered after reworking thumbnails for trust signals: views 2.8x, recommendations 5x, revenue 6.6x.

Across 32,000+ videos from 93 made for kids YouTube channels, 10% more visual motion went with about 1% more views; in a field test, gentle moving background elements (drifting stars) lifted view rates 1.6 to 2%.
leaves.src: Information Systems Research via Deccan Chronicle, Oct 2026

leaves.t: Eye tracking of 6 to 10 year olds showed background motion does not stop kids looking away but brings them back faster; most extra attention went to the background, so motion should support the song's action, not distract from it.
leaves.src: ISB study via Deccan Chronicle, Oct 2026

leaves.t: Slow media is gaining ground: experts now urge parents to judge kids shows by pace, naming Cocomelon and other rapid fire shows; a calm but always gently moving scene fits both the algorithm and parents.
Infants look at faces equally whether they are centred or at the edge of the frame, while older viewers expect the main face centred; keep the lead Bro centred and big for mixed age audiences.
Moonbug partnered with UCLA researchers in 2026 to answer 'addictive' and overstimulation criticism of CoComelon, showing that pacing and wellbeing are now a brand trust issue for big kids channels.

In vidIQ's study of 500 breakout thumbnails (Jun 2026), a face appeared in 80% of the top 50 and a face or strong contrast in 92%, while exaggerated expressions appeared in only 6%, so a big, clear, happy Bro face beats an extreme reaction.

72% of breakout thumbnails used overlay text with a median of 5 words, but 28% used none; for preschool viewers who cannot read, we keep text to 3 words or fewer and let the face and object tell the story.

Animaj keeps characters strictly on model across episodes and uses an AI assisted in between tool so animators spend their time on expressive performance (for example ear timing to show a feeling); consistent, expressive characters are the asset.
Animal families, vehicles (bus, car, trucks), and everyday routines (brushing teeth, bath, bedtime) are evergreen hits.
Tooth-brushing videos get a seasonal boost around October (Halloween candy).
Farm machines and 'satisfying' efficiency videos are popular with kids.
Learning in disguise (phonics, numbers, colours inside a fun song) is a top trend; ChuChu's Phonics Song is India's most-viewed video (5.8B).
Cute kids plus cute pets push views even higher.
Dogs, dinosaurs, big machines/vehicles, community helpers (firefighters, doctors) and animals are the subjects toddlers ask for again and again.
Kids feel powerless in real life, so simple problems the characters solve themselves (rescue, find, fix) give them a sense of mastery.
Daily routines (bath, potty, washing hands, bedtime) are among the most-watched kids songs ever: Cocomelon's Bath Song has about 7.5B views.

Holiday calendar for the next weeks: Hanukkah starts 4 Dec 2026, St Nicholas Day 6 Dec, Colombia's Day of Little Candles 7 Dec, St Lucia 13 Dec, Las Posadas 16 to 24 Dec, Christmas 25 Dec, Kwanzaa from 26 Dec, then New Year.
Lights and candles run through almost every December festival (Hanukkah, Velitas, St Lucia, Posadas, Christmas), so a 'twinkle lights' theme celebrates many cultures without picking one.

Worldwide interest in holiday music jumps the day after Halloween and with the first cold snaps, then climbs through November, so festive and winter kids songs should be live by the second half of November.

December is the long summer school break in Brazil, Argentina, Australia and South Africa; snow themes do not fit there, so pair each winter song with a sunny summer or beach version for southern audiences.
Holiday neutral winter fun (snowflakes, mittens, hot cocoa, baking cookies; National Cookie Day is 4 Dec) works across religions and keeps content usable after the holidays end.
Ramadan 2027 is likely to start about 8 Feb and Eid al Fitr about 9 or 10 Mar 2027; moon, lantern and sharing songs for Arabic and Indonesian audiences should be ready by late January.
Safety and habit songs parents search for (seatbelt, dentist visit, road crossing, manners) are among the fastest growing kids topics on Shorts in 2026.
US Thanksgiving is Thursday 26 Nov 2026: thankfulness and harvest songs (sharing food, saying thank you to family) peak in the next 10 days.
Lunar New Year 2027 falls on Saturday 6 Feb, the Year of the Goat (Sheep); a friendly goat dance song and red lantern visuals should be ready by late January for East and Southeast Asian audiences.

Gen Alpha 3 to 8 year olds' favourite characters in 2026: superheroes (Spider-Man, Superman, Batman), Bluey, Barbie, Elsa, Moana, Sonic, SpongeBob and Paw Patrol's Chase; heroes, speed, and brave adventure are the shared themes we can echo with original characters.
Games are now the third biggest way young kids discover new characters, after TV and movies and ahead of toys, so playable moments (dance games, guessing, choices) build attachment.
68% of parents say their child loves some of the same characters they loved as kids; content parents enjoy co watching (gentle humour, nostalgic sounds) gets replayed in family time.

Netflix's No. 1 English film for 2 to 8 Nov 2026 was A Dog's Perfect Christmas (8.6M views), a talking dog family holiday film, showing that dog plus Christmas stories pull families from early November.
UN World Children's Day is Friday 20 Nov 2026 (India's Children's Day was 14 Nov); a song about kids everywhere playing, sharing and being friends fits the week and travels across countries.
Christmas Day 2026 falls on a Friday, giving most families a three day weekend; our weekly Friday compilation should be a holiday mega mix that day and on New Year's Day (also a Friday).

Playful December days to hook songs on: International Mountain Day (11 Dec), Wright Brothers Day (17 Dec, a flying plane song), Ugly Christmas Sweater Day (18 Dec, a silly sweater dance) and Cut Out Snowflakes Day (27 Dec, a craft along song).
Bodhi Day (8 Dec, Buddhist) and Iceland's Christmas Eve book flood tradition (24 Dec, gifting books and reading) are gentle, low competition themes for a calm reading or kindness song.
Infobells (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu channels) and ChuChu TV lead Indian kids content; Hindi rhymes like Lakdi Ki Kathi have 4B views.
Regional-language versions (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu) each build channels with 30M+ subscribers.
Food-themed content is a reliable way to reach Indian kids on Shorts.

The audience is global: the most-viewed kids channels reach every region by dubbing into many languages (Kids Diana Show alone runs Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, Portuguese, Indonesian, Japanese and German versions).
In an 11 language dubbing test on a kids channel, Spanish, Arabic, Indonesian and Portuguese pulled ahead first (then Japanese and Korean); dubbed audio tracks now bring over 30% of its views.
Dub new uploads at release and most of the back catalogue: viewers who liked one dubbed video left when nothing else was in their language; that channel dubbed about 70% of its catalogue.

Audio quality decides whether dubbing helps: on an Italian kids channel weak AI dubs cut average watch time to under 1 minute versus 5 to 6 minutes for professional dubs, and can pull the whole channel down.
Cheap demand test before dubbing: translate titles and descriptions of the top 20% of videos into many languages and watch 60 days of views by country and audio language.

Multi language audio on one channel amplifies signals the channel already has; separate language channels start from zero (Vania Mania's own Portuguese channel underperformed until it became an audio track).

El Reino Infantil (Argentina) is the biggest Spanish kids network: 180 billion lifetime views, 9 billion in H1 2026, audience led by Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Peru and the US, built on named farm animal characters singing preschool songs.
Dubbed tracks can hold kids longer than the original: average view duration was Spanish 8:24 vs English 6:26 (+31%), Portuguese 7:59, Indonesian 7:12, Arabic 6:46.

Indonesia is a kids viewing giant: in one Aug 2026 week five Indonesian, kid friendly family creators sat in the worldwide top 50 (Keizo and Friends #18 with 655M weekly views), even after an under 16 social media ban.

YouTube music royalties per 1,000 streams (Content ID, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026): Canada 9.57 USD, Germany 7.34, UK 5.81, Australia 5.78, US 4.30, Mexico 1.39, Brazil 1.03, India 0.48, Philippines 0.31, Indonesia 0.15.
The biggest kids audiences (India, Indonesia, Philippines, Brazil) pay the least per view, so the winning mix is English songs that travel to high value markets plus dubbed tracks for volume markets.

In Inflr's Oct 2026 ranking of Brazilian channels that engage kids, the animated music brand Mundo Bita ranks 3rd (14.5M subs, 22.9B views) above creators with 50M subs, and Turma da Monica is 5th, so animated song brands compete equally with star creators in Brazil.

Seven of Brazil's top nine kids channels sell licensed products (toys, books, school supplies), and six of the top 30 build on Minecraft or Roblox; Brazilian kids reward recurring characters they can buy and play with.

Brazilian kids pop is booming: MC Divertida has 8.6B plays and 18M subs with a strong preschool audience, and the duo Kysha e Mine passed 1.2B YouTube views and 130M TikTok likes in about a year; upbeat pop sung by kids works in Portuguese.
Brazil's leading kids music producers have lyrics and scripts checked by teams that include psychologists and keep a general audience rating, which they say builds trust with parents and teachers.
YouTube's quality principles push high-quality made-for-kids videos up in recommendations and decide entry to the YouTube Kids app.
Six low-quality types to avoid: heavily promotional, negative behaviour, fake-educational, hard to follow/mass-produced, sensational or keyword-stuffed, odd use of familiar characters.
Red flags: flashing lights, loud or sudden sounds, chaotic camera moves, rushed storytelling, mean characters even as jokes.
YouTube is cracking down on low-effort AI 'slop' for kids; originality and consistent quality matter more in 2026.
Getting into the YouTube Kids app is done through review (often via an official YouTube partner), not by applying directly.

There is no public banned word list, but words in six risk clusters (fear, conflict, medical, danger, emotional overload like 'shocking', adult themes like 'crush') lower kids recommendations and ads.

Kids and teens has the lowest median RPM of 13 niches, about 0.33 USD per 1,000 views versus about 2.30 overall (300 channels, May 2025 to May 2026), so kids channels win on volume and long watch sessions.

YouTube requires disclosing AI generated music (its detector does not scan soundtracks, so it is on us); clearly animated or unreal visuals need no label, and for animated work the label sits in the expanded description and does not cut reach.
Since 27 May 2026 YouTube auto applies AI labels to undeclared photorealistic AI; repeated failure to disclose can lead to removal or Partner Program suspension.

YouTube's Jul 2026 inauthentic content update names three non monetisable types: generic or repetitive template series with the same situations and outcomes, unsatisfying shock or stitched AI clips, and AI 'experts' on sensitive topics; a clear original creative spin keeps AI assisted work safe.

The FTC's amended COPPA Rule compliance date was 22 Apr 2026: every video needs an audience setting, YouTube's classifier can mark videos as for kids (appeal only), and Disney paid 10M USD partly for labelling whole channels instead of each video.
Made for kids channels are excluded from YouTube Shopping affiliates and lose personalised ads, comments and notifications, so revenue depends on views and watch time volume.

Suno songs can only be monetised if made on a paid plan (Pro or Premier) at the time of creation; fully AI songs get no copyright, so adding our own written lyrics and arrangement edits protects the human parts. Keep receipts and creation dates per song.
Suno settled with Warner Music and is moving to licensed models with monthly download caps; current v5 models will be phased out, so back up the full song catalogue now.

YouTube Kids entry runs through automated filters that read thumbnails, titles and the video itself, plus human spot checks and parent reports; paid placements, purchase pushing and toy packaging videos are excluded.

leaves.t: YouTube's Mar 2026 Dublin summit treats kids and teens as separate audiences and signals that YouTube Kids will favour less overstimulating, authentic, human made content over mindless AI output.

Songs released as YouTube Music Art Tracks through a distributor earn much more per 1,000 streams than Content ID claims (UK 18.87 USD, Germany 14.05, US 11.22), a second income stream for our Suno songs made on the paid plan.

YouTube's five high quality traits for kids content are kindness and healthy habits, curiosity and learning, creativity and imaginative play, life skills with clear lessons, and diverse people and places; videos with them are promoted in recommendations.
Quality is judged at two levels: a single low quality video gets limited or no ads, while a channel that focuses on low quality content can be suspended from the Partner Program.
'Deceptively educational' is a named low quality type: a title or thumbnail that promises learning must deliver accurate learning in the video, so 'learn colours' songs must really teach colours.
'Hard to follow' storylines count as low quality, so each song should tell one clear, simple story from start to finish.

Even large kids channels (PlayToys, 8M subs) can be missing from the YouTube Kids app; after a partner escalated to YouTube's review team on 20 May, the Kids team approved them by 18 Jun, after which they became searchable and appeared as suggestions.

YouTube Kids filtering (Team YouTube FAQ, 1 Apr 2026) works in layers: automated filters read thumbnails, titles and the video itself, human reviewers spot check and refine the filters, and parent flags are reviewed around the clock and removed for everyone if upheld.

YouTube Kids excludes paid product placements, videos that push purchases, packaging and unboxing focused videos and excessive accumulation or consumption of products, so our songs should never feature branded toys or buying.
YouTube renamed the Partner Program's 'repetitious content' rule to 'mass produced content' on 15 Jul 2025; with 14 songs a week we must keep each song clearly different in story, setting and moves.
Community Guidelines strikes: a first violation is usually a warning that expires after 90 days with policy training; three strikes within 90 days can terminate the channel.
YouTube Kids added over 100 Sesame Street episodes in Jan 2026, so trusted educational brands are now direct competitors on the YouTube Kids learning shelf.
YouTube channel stands at about 2,140 subscribers with 450 to 1,400 views a day in 1 to 15 Nov 2026; the best days (10 and 12 Nov) followed the Jungle Doctors song and a Hindi Didi story.

Top long form uploads 1 to 15 Nov: Lion Needs a Doctor (833 views), Light the Diyas (783), Ek Diya Sabke Liye (456), Stomp Your Boot hoedown (382), Dhol Bajao (356), Who Took the Cookie (319): story songs with a problem to fix and festival songs lead.

Average view duration on our long form songs is only about 15 to 25 seconds; cartoon episodes hold a little longer (up to 36 s for Buddy's Birthday) but get fewer views, so early retention is our biggest weakness.
Our YouTube Shorts get almost no views (1 to 30 each) while the same moments on Instagram Reels get 50 to 125, so YouTube is not yet testing our Shorts with seed audiences.

Instagram Reels lose 58 to 90% of viewers in the first 3 seconds; the lowest skip rates were the Wave Jump Hop action song (58%), the Sports Day race (59%) and a Hindi Didi cloud story (59%), the highest were Diwali Dhamaka (90%) and Buddy's Birthday episode (88%).
Likes, comments and shares are near zero on both platforms (best: 3 shares for Jalao Deep on Instagram), so watch and skip behaviour is the only real signal we get.
Reel views were about 100 to 125 each in the first week of November but mostly 20 to 90 after 9 Nov, so Instagram reach is softening and the hook needs to improve.
Given our Shorts get almost no YouTube views, the data points to fewer, better Shorts cut fresh from each song's most energetic moment, rather than more volume.

leaves.t: Metricool's per video YouTube data runs about 4 days behind (on 15 Nov the newest row was the 11 Nov upload), so judge each song only after 4 or 5 days, not on its first day.

Even for an Indian festival, the English titled Diwali song Light the Diyas reached 783 views while the Hindi titled Jalao Deep rock song reached only 69, so English titles reach a wider audience for us.
Our songs outperform our cartoon episodes about 3 to 1 on views (songs mostly 100 to 830, episodes mostly 10 to 220) with similar 15 to 36 second average watch, so songs should stay the core output.

The 10 AM IST song uploads hold most of our top results (Lion Needs a Doctor, Light the Diyas, Ek Diya, Stomp Your Boot, Dhol Bajao), while 4 PM slots, often episodes, trail; content type and slot are mixed so the slot effect is not proven.

Simple sing along manner songs did modestly (Thank You 197, Zoo Stomp 102, Birthday Shake 49) compared with songs built around a small problem or mission (Lion doctor 833, Cookie mystery 319, Treasure hunt 251).
Instagram Reels posted 9 to 14 Nov got only 5 to 91 views each, down from about 100 to 125 in early November, so our Instagram reach has kept falling for two weeks.

The best Reels that week were the mystery (Who Took the Cookie, 91 views), the bedtime shy monster lullaby (65) and the pirate treasure hunt (62): a question or a little mystery in the first line pulls more viewers than an action list.

Average Reel watch time is mostly 2 to 4 seconds; the exceptions were Blast Off space bus (about 14 s), the Hindi grumpy cloud story (about 12 s) and the giant pumpkin garden song (about 9 s), all with a clear transformation (rocket launch, rain, seed to pumpkin).
Saves and shares on our Reels are still zero across the week, so nothing yet makes parents send our Reels to others, the strongest Instagram reach signal.

playbook: Major key, 4/4, 110-125 BPM for dance songs; keep one slow 60-70 BPM wind-down song in the week.
One 1-2 bar hook repeated in every chorus, simple melody inside about 5 notes; add nonsense syllables (la la, doo doo) kids can sing before they can talk.
Every lyric line has an action kids can copy (Total Physical Response): clap, jump, wiggle, freeze, stomp.
Use call-and-response or riddle lines ('What colour? RED!') with a short pause so kids can answer at home.

A tiny story that is easy to follow (one problem, one fix, one clear lesson such as kindness or a healthy habit) with one tempo change kids can act out, ending in a happy payoff; show people and places from many cultures.
A child's voice as the lead singer; characters look into the camera and talk to the viewer.

Subjects: family, animals, dogs, dinosaurs, vehicles, helpers, pretend play jobs and daily routines; each week make 2 songs as fresh Bro Bros twists on public domain rhymes (Wheels on the Bus, Old MacDonald, Five Little Ducks) with an animal or job twist and a learning tag in the title.

Half step key lift for the final chorus; start each song with a 2 bar clap or drum pattern (rhythm hooks babies first) and colour the arrangement with bright high register sounds (bells, xylophone, ukulele).

Camera and motion: calm cuts every 3 to 6 s, lead Bro centred and big, gentle constant background motion (drifting clouds, bubbles, stars) that matches the song, bright rounded visuals, big friendly eyes; no flashing, no sudden loud sounds.

Hide one learning point (counting, colours, routine, feelings, safety) and name it in the description; at least one song a week should be a healthy habit or safety song parents search for (dentist, seatbelt, crossing the road, manners).

Shorts and Reels: our skip rate in the first 3 s is 58 to 90%, so open on full body dancing at the chorus peak or a direct action call (wave, jump, race), never on slow setup; make each Short a new cut with its own hook and loop back to the start.

Thumbnails: one happy face, one clear action, one recognisable object, big eyes, max 3 words, bright plain background; never scared, crying or shocked faces; test changes by hand because Test and Compare is off for kids videos.

Weekly long form: one 10 to 20 minute compilation (5 or 6 songs, best performer first) every Friday, the strongest kids upload day; keep a 24/7 live stream of all songs running and point stream playlists back to new uploads.

Languages: add re-sung audio tracks (not low quality AI voice swaps) to the best songs in Spanish, Portuguese, Indonesian and Arabic first, then Hindi; translate titles and descriptions of the top songs into 20 languages to test demand; keep one channel with multi audio rather than new language channels.

Originality and compliance: write our own lyrics, vary story situations and endings week to week (no template clones), tick the AI music disclosure on every upload, set made for kids per video, and make every Suno song on the paid plan.

Mix in older kid energy: at least two songs a week should be full body dance alongs (Danny Go! style) with a funny chantable nonsense word kids can shout; group Shorts of the same song family into a YouTube Shorts series and, once we pass 1,000 Instagram followers, test two hooks per song with Trial Reels.

Titles: story hook plus an age keyword (for toddlers, learn numbers 1-10, bedtime for preschoolers), max 2 caps words and 1 to 2 emojis, no fear, fight, medical or danger words; put every video in a keyword playlist and link the playlist's first video in the description.

Seasonal plan: until 24 Dec post at least 3 holiday neutral winter or lights songs a week (snow, cookies, twinkle lights), each with a sunny summer variant for the southern hemisphere; start Ramadan and Lunar New Year friendly songs in January.

log.note: Run 1: seeded 38 learnings across 8 branches (platforms, top channels, music, visuals, topics, India, YouTube rules). First 9 playbook rules.
Run 2 (YouTube algorithm): new branch with 12 learnings on how Home, Suggested, Search, Shorts and Reels rank videos; 3 new playbook rules. Total 50.

Run 3 (deep dive: music + what kids love): 21 learnings from music preference studies, Super Simple Songs, Ms. Rachel, Blue's Clues, thumbnails and top kids topics. Playbook rewritten to 15 rules; 14 song ideas for next week. Total 72.

Run 4 (other platforms): Netflix kids data: CoComelon fell out of the Netflix kids top 10 while creator shows (Ms. Rachel, Danny Go!, Sheriff Labrador) grew; movement songs travel; Spotify now lets parents hide kids music from their own taste profile; nonsense chants like Chicken Banana spread on TikTok and Reels. Total 80.

Run 5 (music craft): New infant music studies: 12 month olds move to real songs but not in time, higher pitch draws more brain response and movement, rhythm is innate while melody is learned; babies like young voices and sing song speech; Pinkfong Bebefinn formula of short looping songs. Total 87.

Run 6 (visual craft): Thumbnails and titles for kids: YouTube Test and Compare is blocked for made for kids videos; thumbnail formula of one happy face, one action, one item; titles with a story hook plus an age keyword; risky word clusters; playlists as main discovery; short clips only grow distinctive characters. Total 95.

Run 7 (topics and seasons): Next 4 weeks calendar: Hanukkah from 4 Dec, St Nicholas 6 Dec, Velitas 7 Dec, St Lucia 13 Dec, Las Posadas 16 Dec, Christmas, Kwanzaa; holiday music interest climbs from the day after Halloween; December is summer break in the southern hemisphere; Ramadan 2027 likely from 8 Feb. Total 101.

Run 8 (global markets): Dubbing data: in an 11 language kids test Spanish, Arabic, Indonesian and Portuguese pulled ahead and dubbed tracks gave over 30% of views; poor AI dubs crushed watch time; multi audio beats new channels when demand exists; El Reino Infantil leads Spanish kids content with audiences led by Mexico and Argentina. Total 107.

Run 9 (competitors Bebefinn and Lalafun): Bebefinn: about 84M subs brand wide, 370M views a month on the main channel, top hits are a morning routine, a Baby Shark crossover, a mix and a car chase. Lalafun: a 3D channel born Oct 2022 now at 15M subs and 600M+ views a month from animal twists on public domain rhymes plus learning tags. Total 114.

Run 10 (algorithm experiments and data): Timing and format data for kids channels: Friday is the best day and Wednesday the worst (+379% gap), 10 to 20 minute videos suit the niche; 24/7 streams of the back catalogue drive up to 42% of watch time at higher RPM; YouTube Kids app can supply two thirds of traffic; dubbed Spanish tracks hold viewers longer than English. Total 122.

Run 11 (rules, safety, monetisation): AI labels: AI generated music must be disclosed (detection does not catch soundtracks) while clearly animated visuals do not need a label; inauthentic content rules demonetise template driven repetition; COPPA amendments took effect 22 Apr 2026 with per video audience labels (Disney paid 10M USD); Suno music needs a paid plan for monetisation and fully AI songs get no copyright. Total 129.

Run 12 (our own results): First real Metricool read for 1 to 15 Nov: about 2,140 YouTube subs and 450 to 1,400 daily views; story problem songs and Diwali songs led; average view duration only about 15 to 25 s; YouTube Shorts nearly unseen while Reels get 50 to 125 views; Reels lose 58 to 90% of viewers in the first 3 s. Total 136.

Run 13 (YouTube main and Kids charts): Tubefilter weekly top 50: VocaVoca, a US Shorts led kids song channel built on healthy habits and safety songs, jumped from about 0.5B monthly views in May to 2.9B in Oct 2026; Indian family channels rode Diwali; YouTube keeps autoplay off and break reminders on by default for under 18s. Total 141.

Run 14 (YouTube algorithm official): Todd Beaupre (Sep 2026): new uploads are tested on mixed audiences including non subscribers from the first hour, each audience is judged separately, about 10% subscriber click rate is normal. YouTube Kids FAQ (Apr 2026): filters read thumbnails, titles and video; no product placement; new profiles see curated shelves until history builds. Total 147.

Run 15 (Shorts and Reels algorithm): Shorts: seed audience loop, no ideal length or posting time per YouTube, stalled Shorts need a new Short not a repost, Shorts series and custom thumbnails added in 2026. Reels: 55% of views come from non followers, DM sends weigh 3 to 5x likes, Trial Reels for 1,000+ follower accounts, aggregator penalty for 70%+ reused visuals or audio. Total 153.

Run 16 (other platforms): YouTube reaches 67% of US kids aged 2 to 5 and 80% of 10 to 12; streamer kids trends are edutainment inside stories, interactive choices and short flexible viewing; Netflix preschool is the most crowded category (PAW Patrol, Gabby's Dollhouse, Ms. Rachel, Sesame Street); Roblox reaches 61% of UK 8 to 14s. Total 157.

Run 17 (music craft): Rhythm together boosts preschool behaviour (RAMSR study, 200+ four year olds); Danny Go! builds songs as dance games (freeze, fast vs slow, imaginary danger, hyperspeed remixes); CoComelon now uses music as its main teaching tool with a UCLA learning framework; singing builds vocabulary. Total 163.

Run 18 (visual craft): New ISB study of 32,000 kids videos: 10% more visual motion links to about 1% more views and pulls wandering eyes back faster, but more animation is not better for learning; slow media movement keeps growing; young infants look at faces anywhere in frame while older viewers expect the face centred. Total 168.

Run 19 (topics and seasons): US Thanksgiving is 26 Nov; Lunar New Year 2027 is 6 Feb, Year of the Goat; Gen Alpha 3 to 8 favourites are superheroes, Bluey, Barbie, Elsa, Sonic and SpongeBob; games are now the third way kids discover characters; parents love sharing favourites. Total 173.

Run 20 (global markets): Indonesia: five Indonesian, kid friendly creators in a single Tubefilter weekly top 50 despite an under 16 social media ban. Music royalty rates per 1,000 streams show rich markets (Canada, Germany, UK, Australia, US) pay 10 to 60 times more than India, Indonesia and the Philippines; Art Tracks pay far more than Content ID. Total 177.

Run 21 (competitor ChuChu TV): ChuChu TV (Chennai) now reports 180M+ digital subscribers and 110B views and signed a worldwide Netflix deal (Sep 2026) for four collections in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu, aiming to become a global preschool franchise; its main English channel crossed 50M subs. Total 181.

Run 22 (algorithm experiments and data): Two kids channel experiments: WOA Song Spanish removed policy risky long videos and posted 31 quality checked Shorts in a quarter, views went from 27M to 1.46B with Shorts at 98% of views; another channel halved long form, doubled Shorts cut from its best moments and moved to 4K TV friendly quality, revenue up 34%. Total 186.

Run 23 (rules, safety, monetisation): Re checked YouTube's official kids and family quality principles: five high quality traits (kindness and healthy habits, curiosity and learning, creativity and play, life skills with clear lessons, diverse people and places) are promoted in recommendations and YouTube Kids; a channel focused on low quality content can lose the Partner Program. Total 190.

Run 24 (our own results): Fresh Metricool read: analytics for published videos lag about 4 days (latest row 11 Nov while uploads continue daily); English Diwali song Light the Diyas got 783 views against 69 for the Hindi Diwali rock song; songs beat cartoon episodes about 3 to 1 on views; 10 AM IST song slots lead. Run 25 (YouTube main and Kids charts): Tubefilter week of 8 Nov: 37 of the top 50 subscriber gainers live mainly on Shorts; kids entries are Pokemon Kids TV, Cadel and Mia and VocaVoca; Pokemon Kids TV's top songs are single character dance songs; Sasha Show's 9.5M sub October came from borrowed characters and shock titles, a pattern to avoid; YouTube Kids entry for PlayToys took about 4 weeks via partner review. Run 26 (YouTube algorithm): Sept 2026 inauthentic content suspensions hit long one template sleep music and prayer compilations; Oct 2026 brought saved custom Home feeds and Ask YouTube answers in the US; creator analysis says the recommender now targets satisfied watch time per click and gives fewer long form slots on Home, so old Shorts fade and fresh varied work matters. Total 207.

Run 27 (Shorts and Reels): Instagram's Your Algorithm topic controls now cover Reels, Explore (Apr 2026) and Feed (Jun 2026), so clear topic signals matter; guidance favours motion or text within half a second, keyword captions over hashtags, on screen text for AI topic reading and about 90% niche consistency; near duplicate penalties last 24 hours to 30 days. Total 211.

Run 28 (other platforms): Baby Shark passed 1 billion Spotify streams (May 2026) at about 400K a day led by US, UK, Australia and Canada; Netflix kids top 10s show YouTube creator CrunchLabs breaking in, KPop Demon Hunters still charting at week 65, and a Christmas dog family film at No. 1 in early November; KIDZ BOP uses a Roblox obstacle game to reach Gen Alpha. Run 29 (music craft): Infants' movement follows changes in loudness and intensity rather than the beat, so build clear loud and soft contrasts; familiar songs hold babies longer even when a stranger sings at a different tempo; November kids album charts are led by a gentle jazz Christmas soundtrack, movie musicals and only three YouTube born brands. Total 219.

Run 30 (visual craft): vidIQ's July 2026 study of 500 breakout thumbnails: faces in 80% of the top 50, face or strong contrast in 92%, extreme expressions in only 6%; Animaj's new preschool series Ozzy Fox builds every episode on one original song that turns a routine into a mission and hit 1.5M views in under 5 days. Run 31 (topics and seasons): Next dates: UN World Children's Day on 20 Nov; Christmas 2026 is a Friday, so our Friday compilation lands on Christmas Day; fun December hooks are Ugly Christmas Sweater Day (18 Dec), Wright Brothers Day (17 Dec, planes), International Mountain Day (11 Dec) and Cut Out Snowflakes Day (27 Dec). Run 32 (global markets): Brazil: an Oct 2026 Inflr ranking puts animated music brand Mundo Bita third (14.5M subs, 22.9B views) ahead of far bigger creators, with Turma da Monica also top 5; seven of the top nine have licensed products; Brazilian kids pop (MC Divertida 8.6B plays, Kysha e Mine 1.2B views in a year) grows across YouTube and TikTok. Run 34 (algorithm experiments and data): Two more kids channel cases: The Melobies (energetic nursery rhymes) grew subscribers over 9 times after YouTube Kids listing, expressive high contrast mobile thumbnails, keyword titles, themed playlists and 24/7 streams; Sandy the Sticker went from 1 to 16 automated 24/7 streams and added Shorts cut from long form, lifting watch time 31% and average view duration from 1:36 to 2:06.
